name: Andover High School Environmental Club
description: Student club at Andover High School that runs recycling, composting, garden and e-waste projects and helps other schools start composting.

name: Alternatives for Community and Environment
description: Roxbury-based environmental justice organization, founded in 1994, that does community organizing, youth leadership, transit advocacy and legal support for low-income communities and communities of color.

name: Massachusetts Interfaith Power & Light
description: Faith-based nonprofit, founded in 2002, that helps houses of worship cut emissions and organizes people of faith for climate advocacy and climate justice.

events.name: Hope Takes Root: Creation Care Service Day and Tree Planting

projects: Energy Audits, Solar and Weatherization for Houses of Worship
actions: Volunteer to plant trees at Hope Takes Root (Oct 3, Lawrence)

projects: ECA Mass legislative advocacy and monthly chapter meetings

name: Greenroots
description: Chelsea environmental justice organization, about 30 years old, that restores salt marsh, builds parks and waterfront access and works to improve Chelsea Creek water quality, with a youth leadership program.

name: Canton Residents for a Sustainable Equitable Future
Cooperative, Energy, Recycling, and Organics Cooperative
description: Worker-owned commercial composting cooperative in Dorchester that collects food waste from businesses and institutions and sends it to local farms for composting.

projects: CERO composting and organic waste collection

name: Environmental League of Massachusetts
description: Statewide environmental policy nonprofit, about 128 years old, that advocates on clean energy, transportation, building efficiency, environmental justice and land protection, and runs the NetZeroMA accountability hub.

name: Hands Across the River Coalition, Inc.
description: New Bedford grassroots group that monitors the cleanup of the PCB-contaminated Acushnet River and New Bedford Harbor Superfund site and educates residents about the health effects of the contamination.

name: No Fracked Gas in Mass
description: Grassroots campaign, run as a program of the Berkshire Environmental Action Team, that opposes gas pipeline projects, follows federal (FERC) pipeline proceedings and promotes clean energy alternatives.

projects: Pipeline and energy updates at BEAT (formerly No Fracked Gas in Mass)
actions: Sign up for The BEAT News gas and energy alerts

name: Resonant Energy
description: Boston-based B Corp solar developer that builds solar for affordable housing, nonprofits, schools and houses of worship, with most projects in Environmental Justice communities.

projects: Solar for affordable housing and nonprofits (Resonant Energy)

name: Take Back the Grid
description: Campaign launched in 2019 by the Boston chapter of Democratic Socialists of America for a community-controlled, publicly accountable energy grid under the banner of energy democracy.

name: Community Action Works
description: Environmental justice nonprofit, founded in 1987, that trains and organizes local groups and gives emergency grants to stop and clean up local pollution such as pipelines, landfills, incinerators and PFAS.

projects: Community Action Works organizing support and training

name: Citizens Climate Lobby
description: Boston-area chapter of Citizens' Climate Lobby whose volunteers start climate conversations, build support among community leaders and meet members of Congress about bipartisan climate policy.

name: Mass Facilities Administrators Association
description: Professional association founded in 1973 for municipal facilities administrators (about 180 members from 140 municipalities) offering training and information exchange.

name: Vermont Natural Resources Council
description: Statewide environmental nonprofit in Montpelier working on climate and clean energy, water, forests and wildlife, transportation and sustainable communities. It coordinates VECAN and Transportation for Vermonters.

actions: 2027 legislative intern (VNRC / Vermont Conservation Voters / Vermont Planners Association)

name: Third Act Vermont
description: Volunteer-run Vermont working group of the national Third Act initiative, organizing people over 60 on climate and democracy through regional groups, legislative advocacy and canvassing.

actions: Join a regional group or action team

name: Hunger Free Vermont
description: Anti-hunger and food-security advocacy organization in South Burlington; joined the Environmental Common Agenda as a new partner in 2026 and co-sponsored the 2026 Vermont Changemakers Summit.

name: Champlain Valley Office of Economic Opportunity
description: Burlington community action agency that works on economic, social, racial and environmental justice; an Energy Action Network member.

name: Efficiency Vermont
description: Statewide energy efficiency program (operated by VEIC) offering rebates and services; one of the five supporting organizations of VECAN.

name: Green Mountain Transit
description: Regional public transit provider; a member of Transportation for Vermonters.

name: Marshfield Energy Committee
description: Marshfield's town energy committee, which posts regular meeting minutes on the town website.

name: Lake Champlain Chamber
description: Regional chamber of commerce for the Burlington and Lake Champlain area, listed as a non-profit member of Energy Action Network.

name: Vermont Futures Project
description: Nonprofit that uses data to bring people together on economic development, environmental sustainability and social justice; it published a statewide Economic Action Plan in January 2025.

name: Craftsbury Energy Committee
description: Town committee whose mission is to guide Craftsbury and its residents toward a more sustainable energy future; it meets at Craftsbury Town Hall.

name: Jericho Energy Task Force
description: Jericho town energy task force that held public meetings through 2026, with agendas posted on the town's Agenda Center.

name: Brandon Energy Committee
description: Subcommittee of the Brandon Planning Commission created in 2018 that wrote the town energy plan and helped put solar panels on the police department.

name: 350Montpelier Node
description: 350Vermont node of activists in the Montpelier area who mobilize and educate people to act for climate justice.
